prompt: Why do the authors say the balance-sheet case study shows that average-quality scoreboards can be misleading about which model to use?

private.model_answer: Gemini and Opus produced functionally equivalent balance sheets, scoring 100% and 95%, but Gemini cost $3.00 and Opus $83.05. A scoreboard of average scores hides this 27.7x gap in cost per correct output, which matters when the task is routine workbook wiring rather than deep reasoning.

rubric.criterion: States that the two models reached similar quality (100% vs 95%)
Concludes that score alone hides cost per correct output
